summaryTr: Political debate over troop deployment to the Strait of Hormuz is intensifying.

editorial.bodyTr: The political controversy surrounding the deployment to the Strait of Hormuz and the complex pending issues in South Korea-U.S. relations require careful examination. editorials.titleTr: [Editorial] Opposition Rejects All Witnesses in Kim Seung-won Hearing, Admits It Cannot Defend Against Allegations
summaryTr: Ruling party refuses all witnesses at confirmation hearing for Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won
Allegations of new drug bribery, stock price manipulation, and court lobbying raised at gate-level scale
Opposition party designates evasion tactic as inability to defend against allegations, demands verification
editorials.bodyTr: The ruling party's outright rejection of all witness testimony ahead of the confirmation hearing for Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won is fueling growing controversy. As gate-level allegations have surfaced surrounding the nominee—including suspected solicitation of clinical trials for new drugs, collusion with stock manipulation forces, and apparent court lobbying—the opposition is demanding thorough vetting and characterizing the current situation as an evasion stemming from an inability to defend against the suspicions.

editorial.body: 입력 15일로 예정된 김승원 법무부 장관 후보자 인사청문회를 놓고 여야가 벌인 증인·참고인 채택 논의가 어제 무산됐다. 국민의힘은 김 후보자를 둘러싼 의혹을 확인하기 위해 48명의 증인·참고인을 요구했지만, 더불어민주당은 “한 명의 증인도 세울 수 없다”는 입장을 고수했다고 한다. 인사청문회는 후보자가 해당 직무를 수행할 자격과 도덕성을 갖췄는지 국민 앞에서 검증하는 자리다. 특히 법치를 책임지는 법무장관은 제기된 의혹이 있다면 사실관계를 더욱 엄중하게 따져야 한다. 그런데 김 후보자를 둘러싼 의혹은 한둘이 아니다. 신약 임상 승인 청탁 의혹을 비롯해 검찰 수사 과정에서 기소 의견이 제시됐다가 돌연 기소유예로 바뀐 경위, 주가 조작 세력 관여 의혹 등 의문이 쌓여 있다. 배우자가 운영한 교육시설이 김 후보자 지역구인 수원으로 옮긴 지 얼마 안 돼 발달장애인 활동서비스 제공 기관으로 선정되고 정부 바우처 수익이 급증한 경위도 규명 대상이다. 민주당 논리는 궁색하다. 임상 승인 청탁 의혹은 실패한 사건으로 종결됐는데 야당이 의혹을 부풀린다는 것이다. 그렇다면 오히려 관련 증인을 불러 사실관계를 명확히 밝히면 될 일이다. 그렇게 못 하는 건 진상이 낱낱이 밝혀질 게 두려워서인가. 민주당은 “인사청문회는 증인 없이 하는 게 보통”이라고 하지만 이 역시 설득력이 떨어진다. 2022년 한동훈 당시 법무부 장관 후보자 청문회 때 민주당은 한동수 대검 감찰부장과 임은정 법무부 감찰담당관을 증인으로 요구해 증언대에 세운 것을 잊었는가. 여당 내에서도 김 후보자 낙마 불가피론이 있지만, 청와대는 “법에 따른 검증 과정”이라며 청문회 절차를 밟아야 한다고 했다. 법에 따른 검증을 한다면서 진상 규명에 필요한 증인·참고인 채택을 막는 행태는 맹탕 청문회로 만들거나 파행으로 몰고 가 임명을 강행하겠다는 속셈 외에는 설명할 길이 없다. 야당이 요구하는 48명의 증인·참고인이 과하다면 핵심 인물 위주로 추려내면 된다. 쏟아지는 의혹들이 사실인지 아닌지, 사실이라면 장관직 수행에 문제가 될 정도인지 아닌지 확인해야 한다는 게 국민의 요구다. 민주당은 증인·참고인 채택에 협조해 의혹의 실체를 밝히는 데 책임을 다해야 한다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Why is the Democratic Party Blocking Witnesses at Kim Seung-won's Confirmation Hearing?
summaryTr: The Democratic Party rejected the adoption of 48 witnesses at the confirmation hearing for Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won.
Multiple allegations have been raised, including suspicions over clinical trial requests for new drugs and the circumstances of prosecutorial suspension.
The attitude of avoiding truth-finding appears to reflect an intent to push ahead with a nominal confirmation hearing.
editorial.bodyTr: Negotiations between the ruling and opposition parties over witness and reference witness appointments for Kim Seung-won's confirmation hearing as justice minister nominee, scheduled for the 15th, fell apart yesterday. The People Power Party requested 48 witnesses and reference witnesses to verify suspicions surrounding Kim, but the Democratic Party reportedly maintained its stance that "not a single witness can be presented." A confirmation hearing is a venue where the nation verifies whether a nominee possesses the qualifications and moral character to perform the relevant duties. Particularly for a justice minister responsible for the rule of law, any raised suspicions should be examined with utmost rigor. Yet the suspicions surrounding Kim are not few. Questions have accumulated, including allegations of improper solicitation regarding drug clinical trial approvals, the circumstances under which prosecutors initially recommended indictment but suddenly changed to deferred prosecution during investigations, and suspicions of involvement by stock manipulation forces. There is also a need to clarify how an educational facility operated by Kim's spouse, shortly after relocating to Suwon where Kim represents, was selected as a developmental disability activity service provider and subsequently saw a sharp increase in government voucher revenues. The Democratic Party's logic is unconvincing. They argue that the clinical trial approval allegations constitute a failed case that has been closed, and that the opposition is inflating suspicions. If that is the case, then calling relevant witnesses to clarify facts would simply resolve the matter. If they cannot do so, it suggests they fear the truth will be fully exposed. The Democratic Party claims that "confirmation hearings are typically conducted without witnesses," but this too lacks persuasive power. Have they forgotten that during Han Dong-hun's justice minister confirmation hearing in 2022, the Democratic Party requested Han Dong-soo, then head of the Supreme Prosecutor's Office's Inspection Division, and Lim Eun-jeong, the Justice Ministry's audit officer, as witnesses and had them testify? Though some within the ruling party suggest Kim's withdrawal is inevitable, the presidential office stated that confirmation procedures should proceed as "a verification process according to law." Blocking the appointment of witnesses and reference witnesses necessary for clarifying the truth while claiming to conduct verification according to law can only be explained as an intention to conduct a perfunctory hearing or turn it into a fiasco while pushing through the appointment. If the 48 witnesses and reference witnesses requested by the opposition are excessive, they can be narrowed down to key figures. Whether the mounting allegations are factual, and if so, whether they would pose problems for ministerial duties—this is what the people demand be verified. The Democratic Party must cooperate in appointing witnesses and reference witnesses and fulfill its responsibility in revealing the substance of these suspicions.

leanScore.rationale: 야당(민주당)의 증인 차단을 강력히 비판하고 법무장관 후보자에 대한 철저한 검증과 법치주의를 강조하는 프레임으로, 여당의 투명성 요구를 지지하는 보수적 입장을 드러냄.

editorial.title: Investigation gap
editorial.body: New investigative agency set to launch amid staffing and equipment shortages A Cheong Wa Dae spokesperson said Tuesday that President Lee Jae Myung nominated lawyer Kim Ji-yong to be the first head of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency, which is scheduled to launch alongside the Prosecution Service on Oct. 2. Kim is a former chief of the Criminal Affairs Department at the Supreme Prosecutors' Office and will lead the agency for two years following a confirmation hearing. A revision to the Criminal Procedure Act pushed through by the Democratic Party of Korea and promulgated by the Lee administration transferred the country’s core investigative functions to the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency. The Prosecution Service will handle prosecutions exclusively 78 years after it was founded. The Lee administration, which dismantled the prosecution through unilateral party legislation despite much concern and opposition, is now appointing a former prosecutor to head the agency, revealing the contradiction of having no choice but to acknowledge the prosecution's investigative capabilities. Moreover, Kim had opposed the abolition of prosecutors' supplementary investigative authority. In 2022, while serving at the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, Kim said that in 30.5 percent of cases in which prosecutors requested supplementary investigations after police were granted authority to close cases themselves, it had taken police more than three months to conduct the supplementary investigations. He expressed concern that if prosecutors' authority to demand supplementary investigations were abolished, the public would bear the full brunt of harm caused by delays in processing cases. We cannot help but ask the fundamental question: Why on earth abolish the prosecution as an institution? The issue of “political prosecutors,” whom the party accused of conducting investigations against it, could have been resolved by establishing a system to correct their behavior. Instead, by eliminating the prosecution as an institution altogether, the party has left the public with no choice but to bear enormous costs and suffer under the new criminal justice system in the years ahead. To make matters worse, hardly any aspect of the operations of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency — from staffing and equipment to organizational structure — can be said to be properly prepared, with just three weeks to go before its launch. The most urgent priority is to secure enough investigators. More than 1,100 positions — 40 percent of its total authorized workforce of 2,874 — remain vacant. According to the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, 615 of the 2,376 prosecutors and prosecution investigators who applied for positions at the agency have withdrawn their applications. The launch preparation task force says it will recruit additional personnel from among police officers, lawyers, accountants and patent attorneys, but a major staffing shortfall has already emerged. Essential computer and communications equipment for investigations is also not expected to be delivered or fully installed until December. The nation’s central investigative agency is set to get off the ground without even having its systems properly in place. Nonetheless, the agency is expected to handle 20,000 to 30,000 cases a year. Moreover, from the moment it opens its doors, it will have to handle specialized investigations that require a high degree of expertise. If cases pile up while there is a shortage of experienced personnel and essential equipment is not fully in place, the agency could be overwhelmed, and its operations could grind to a halt. In the process, many criminals could slip through the legal net, with the public ultimately bearing the cost. This is the fault of the Democratic Party and the Lee administration, which, blinded by the dogma of completely stripping prosecutors of their investigative authority, pushed ahead with dismantling the prosecution without making adequate preparations for the fallout. 새로운 수사기관, 인력·장비 부족 속 출범 예정

청와대 대변인은 지난 화요일 이준석 대통령이 10월 2일 검찰과 함께 출범할 예정인 중대범죄수사청의 초대 청장으로 변호사 김지용을 지명했다고 밝혔다. 김지용은 대검찰청 형사부장을 지낸 전직 검사로, 인준청문회를 거친 후 2년간 기관을 이끌 예정이다.

민주당이 주도해 통과시키고 이 정부가 공포한 형사소송법 개정안은 국가의 핵심 수사 기능을 중대범죄수사청으로 이관했다. 검찰은 창설 78년 만에 처음으로 순수 공소권만을 행사하게 된다.

상당한 우려와 반발에도 불구하고 일방적인 당론 입법으로 검찰을 해체한 이 정부가 이제 전직 검사를 수사청장으로 임명하는 모순을 드러냈으며, 이는 검찰의 수사 능력을 인정할 수밖에 없음을 보여준다. 더욱이 김지용은 검사의 보충수사 청구권 폐지에 반대한 입장을 표해왔다. 2022년 대검찰청에 재직 중일 때 그는 경찰에게 사건 종결권을 부여한 이후 검사가 보충수사를 요청한 사건의 30.5%에서 경찰이 보충수사를 완료하는 데 3개월 이상 소요됐다고 지적했다. 검사의 보충수사 청구권이 폐지될 경우 국민이 사건 처리 지연으로 인한 피해를 전적으로 감수해야 할 것이라는 우려를 표했다.

근본적인 질문을 제기하지 않을 수 없다. 도대체 왜 검찰이라는 제도를 폐지하려는가? 당이 제기해온 '정치검사' 문제는 그들의 행동을 바로잡는 시스템을 구축함으로써 충분히 해결할 수 있었다. 그 대신 검찰 제도 자체를 없앰으로써 당은 국민으로 하여금 향후 수년간 새로운 형사사법제도 하에서 막대한 비용을 감수하고 고통받을 수밖에 없도록 만들었다.

더욱 심각한 것은 출범까지 단 3주를 남긴 시점에서 인력·장비에서부터 조직 구조에 이르기까지 중대범죄수사청의 어떤 운영 측면도 제대로 준비됐다고 보기 어렵다는 점이다. 가장 시급한 과제는 충분한 수사관 확보다. 전체 정원 2,874명의 40%에 해당하는 1,100명 이상의 직책이 공석 상태다. 행정안전부에 따르면 중대범죄수사청에 지원한 2,376명의 검사 및 검찰수사관 중 615명이 지원을 철회했다. 출범 준비 태스크포스는 경찰관, 변호사, 회계사, 변리사 등에서 추가 인력을 모집하겠다고 했지만, 이미 상당한 인력 부족이 발생했다. 수사에 필수적인 컴퓨터 및 통신 장비도 12월까지 납품되거나 완전히 설치되지 않을 것으로 예상된다. 국가의 중앙 수사기관이 기본적인 시스템도 제대로 갖추지 못한 채 출범하려고 한다.

그럼에도 불구하고 수사청은 연간 2만~3만 건의 사건을 처리할 것으로 예상된다. 더욱이 출범 초부터 높은 전문성을 요구하는 특화된 수사를 처리해야 한다. 경험 많은 인력 부족 속에서 사건이 쌓이고 필수 장비가 완전히 갖춰지지 않은 상태에서 수사청은 압도당할 수 있으며, 그 결과 업무가 정지될 수 있다. 이 과정에서 많은 범죄자들이 법의 눈을 피할 수 있으며, 결국 국민이 그 대가를 치르게 된다. 이는 검사의 수사권을 완전히 박탈한다는 교조적 신념에 눈이 멀어 충분한 준비 없이 검찰 해체를 강행한 민주당과 이 정부의 책임이다. 이들은 책임을 져야 한다.

editorials.title: Investigation gap
editorials.body: New investigative agency set to launch amid staffing and equipment shortages A Cheong Wa Dae spokesperson said Tuesday that President Lee Jae Myung nominated lawyer Kim Ji-yong to be the first head of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency, which is scheduled to launch alongside the Prosecution Service on Oct. 2. Kim is a former chief of the Criminal Affairs Department at the Supreme Prosecutors' Office and will lead the agency for two years following a confirmation hearing. A revision to the Criminal Procedure Act pushed through by the Democratic Party of Korea and promulgated by the Lee administration transferred the country’s core investigative functions to the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency. The Prosecution Service will handle prosecutions exclusively 78 years after it was founded. The Lee administration, which dismantled the prosecution through unilateral party legislation despite much concern and opposition, is now appointing a former prosecutor to head the agency, revealing the contradiction of having no choice but to acknowledge the prosecution's investigative capabilities. Moreover, Kim had opposed the abolition of prosecutors' supplementary investigative authority. In 2022, while serving at the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, Kim said that in 30.5 percent of cases in which prosecutors requested supplementary investigations after police were granted authority to close cases themselves, it had taken police more than three months to conduct the supplementary investigations. He expressed concern that if prosecutors' authority to demand supplementary investigations were abolished, the public would bear the full brunt of harm caused by delays in processing cases. We cannot help but ask the fundamental question: Why on earth abolish the prosecution as an institution? The issue of “political prosecutors,” whom the party accused of conducting investigations against it, could have been resolved by establishing a system to correct their behavior. Instead, by eliminating the prosecution as an institution altogether, the party has left the public with no choice but to bear enormous costs and suffer under the new criminal justice system in the years ahead. To make matters worse, hardly any aspect of the operations of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency — from staffing and equipment to organizational structure — can be said to be properly prepared, with just three weeks to go before its launch. The most urgent priority is to secure enough investigators. More than 1,100 positions — 40 percent of its total authorized workforce of 2,874 — remain vacant. According to the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, 615 of the 2,376 prosecutors and prosecution investigators who applied for positions at the agency have withdrawn their applications. The launch preparation task force says it will recruit additional personnel from among police officers, lawyers, accountants and patent attorneys, but a major staffing shortfall has already emerged. Essential computer and communications equipment for investigations is also not expected to be delivered or fully installed until December. The nation’s central investigative agency is set to get off the ground without even having its systems properly in place. Nonetheless, the agency is expected to handle 20,000 to 30,000 cases a year. Moreover, from the moment it opens its doors, it will have to handle specialized investigations that require a high degree of expertise. If cases pile up while there is a shortage of experienced personnel and essential equipment is not fully in place, the agency could be overwhelmed, and its operations could grind to a halt. In the process, many criminals could slip through the legal net, with the public ultimately bearing the cost. This is the fault of the Democratic Party and the Lee administration, which, blinded by the dogma of completely stripping prosecutors of their investigative authority, pushed ahead with dismantling the prosecution without making adequate preparations for the fallout. editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Yellow Envelope Law Opens Door to Safety Negotiations Between Contractors and Subcontractors
summaryTr: Six months into the Yellow Envelope Act, primary contractors and subcontractors have begun negotiations on industrial safety.
Labor-management dialogue for mutual prosperity, previously impossible, is now taking place at worksites.
The Yellow Envelope Act is creating positive changes in the labor sector.
editorial.bodyTr: Six months have passed since the Yellow Envelope Act, an amendment to the Trade Union and Labor Relations Adjustment Act, went into effect on March 10th. Things that would have been unimaginable without the Yellow Envelope Act are now just beginning to unfold—such as primary contractors and subcontractor unions putting their heads together to discuss industrial safety. The Yellow Envelope Act is opening up possibilities for labor-management cooperation in workplaces.

editorial.titleTr: Literacy Crisis Sounds Alarm on National Competitiveness in AI Era
summaryTr: South Korean 15-year-olds' reading proficiency has plummeted to a record low of 501 points.
It has continued to decline over the past 20 years from 556 points, ranking first in 2006.
It signals a warning of weakened national competitiveness in the AI era.
editorial.bodyTr: South Korean students' literacy skills are declining. According to the "Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA 2025)" released on the 8th, the average reading score for Korean 15-year-olds stood at 501 points, marking the lowest level since the country's first participation in 2000. The trend has been downward since peaking at 556 points in 2006, when Korea ranked first. This time, the score dropped by 14 points in just three years. This contrasts sharply with declines of 2 points in science and 5 points in mathematics. Korea's reading ranking among 91 countries has slipped to 3rd to 13th place.
